sections.h2: Which offices handle Grand Rapids property tax?
sections.html:
Two city offices split the work. The City Assessor decides what each parcel is worth, and the City Treasurer sends and collects the bills. Because Grand Rapids is the Kent County seat, the county appears on the winter bill and takes over any balance left unpaid in March.

The treasurer's counter is on the second floor of City Hall, 300 Monroe Ave NW, Suite 220, with phone service at 616-456-3020. The assessor's line is 616-456-3081. The city's BS&A Online site lets anyone look up a parcel or pay without creating an account.

Grand Rapids ranks second in Michigan by population, with an estimated 201,183 people in 2025 on 44.8 square miles of land. It grew beside the Grand River, where a run of rapids once stopped boats, and its addresses carry NE, NW, SE or SW depending on where they fall relative to Fulton Street and Division Avenue. The city lists 37 neighborhoods, among them Heritage Hill, Eastown, Garfield Park and Alger Heights, and all of them are billed the same way.

sections.h2: What are the Grand Rapids tax due dates and late fees?
sections.html:
The summer bill is due July 31 and the winter bill February 14, each shifting to the following business day when it lands on a weekend. Whatever date applies is printed on your bill.

The two bills do different jobs. Summer carries most of the charges: the City, the Kent Intermediate School District, Grand Rapids Community College, the State of Michigan and the State Education Tax. Winter carries county charges only, at rates set by the Kent County Board of Commissioners.

Grand Rapids tax bills, per the City Treasurer's policy page
BillGoes outDuePenalty after due date
SummerFirst week of JulyJuly 311% of the balance per month
WinterFirst week of DecemberFebruary 144%

A missing bill does not cancel the debt. Phone 616-456-3020 for a copy. The city says it does not report late payments to credit bureaus, yet the penalties still apply.

sections.h2: How does the city turn taxable value into a bill?
sections.html:
Everything starts with taxable value, the number the city taxes, which may equal or fall below assessed value. The assessor revisits market value yearly to set both.

  • PRE percentage: the principal residence exemption excuses 18 school operating mills on the portion of the home that is the owner's residence, so a duplex may be split.
  • Millage: mills per $1,000 of taxable value, with the full rate tied to the school district.
  • Administration: a 1% Property Tax Administration Fee is added.
  • Estimator: an online calculator asks for district, taxable value and PRE.

The city's sample bill assumes a $50,000 taxable value, full PRE and the 2017 millage rate for Grand Rapids schools, and it produces $1,729.07 for summer and winter together. Because that rate is old, use the sample only to follow the arithmetic, and read the current rate on the Kent County website.

sections.h2: Where can a Grand Rapids owner dispute a value?
sections.html:
Start in February at the Assessor's Review by filing a petition with the City Assessor. Unhappy with the answer? Appeal in March to the Board of Review, in writing or by appointment. Only owners who already petitioned the assessor may appear in March.

The July and December boards are narrower. They fix qualified errors the assessor has verified for the current and one earlier year, such as a clerical slip, a mutual mistake of fact or a measuring or math error, and they can grant a poverty exemption for the current year alone. MCL 211.53b is the controlling statute.

Waiting for a board does not suspend payment. After the board's final report reaches the treasurer, a corrected bill follows in roughly 30 days, yet the first bill stays due and penalties keep running. Refunds are paid to whoever paid the tax.

sections.h2: Which Grand Rapids homeowners can delay or reduce a payment?
sections.html:
A deferment moves the summer deadline to the winter deadline. The household must earn under $40,000 and the home must be the owner's principal residence, and the owner must also be in one of these groups:

  • Over age 62
  • Paraplegic or quadriplegic
  • Totally and permanently disabled
  • Blind
  • An eligible veteran, service member, or surviving spouse of one

The city typically grants requests and calls only for missing details. Apply online, print the PDF, or visit the treasurer's office. Exemptions for disabled veterans and for poverty exist too, and the Property Tax Payments and Policies page links the steps.

An owner who cannot clear the whole bill can ask about installments, which add a penalty. Renaissance zone residents may qualify for exemptions annually, but a single late property tax payment anywhere in Michigan disqualifies them.

sections.h2: When must a Grand Rapids owner claim the principal residence exemption?
sections.html:
By June 1, with the City Assessor, using the PRE affidavit. MCL 211.7cc requires a qualified owner who lives in the home as a principal residence and triggers no disqualifying rule.

Missing June 1 can sometimes be repaired. The assessor may ask for proof that the owner lived there on that date and then adjust the current year and as many as three prior years.

sections.h2: What happens in Grand Rapids when taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
On March 1 every unpaid real property bill, summer or winter, goes to the Kent County Treasurer, who adds county penalties and a 4% administrative fee. The county can sell parcels more than 24 months delinquent after a court order. Delinquent personal property and most abatement bills stay with the city.

Two checkpoints touch a sale. A recorded warranty deed needs a county treasurer certificate under MCL 211.135 covering the five prior years. The title company also wants a written payoff, which the city treasurer provides for current bills and the Kent County Treasurer for anything past March 1.

An owner facing a balance can list on the market, sell as-is to a cash buyer, or pay it down first. Collect written payoff numbers before choosing a closing date.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about housing in Grand Rapids?
sections.html:
QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows 80,222 households, a median owner-occupied value of $244,500 and an owner-occupancy rate of 54.0%, below the 65.2% national figure. Median gross rent is $1,266 and median household income is $69,108. About 41.6% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree, and the average commute is 19 minutes.

With nearly half of homes rented, owners of rental parcels should remember that the PRE reaches only the part of a property the owner lives in. The city's Economic Development Department also runs incentive programs for vacant or obsolete property and answers at 616-456-3431.

faqs.q: What day is the Grand Rapids summer tax due?
faqs.a: July 31, or the next business day when that is a weekend. Bills go out in the first week of July, and a 1% charge builds for each month the balance sits unpaid.

faqs.q: Who collects Grand Rapids tax after March 1?
faqs.a: The Kent County Treasurer. Unpaid real property bills leave the city on that date, and the county adds penalties and a 4% administrative fee.

faqs.q: Can Grand Rapids homeowners get extra time on the summer bill?
faqs.a: Some can. A household earning under $40,000 that lives in the home may apply for deferment to the winter date if the owner is over 62, disabled, blind, or an eligible veteran or surviving spouse. Installment plans with a penalty are also offered.

faqs.q: When is the Grand Rapids principal residence exemption deadline?
faqs.a: June 1, filed with the City Assessor. A late filing may still be accepted with proof of owner occupancy on that date, reaching the current year and up to three earlier ones.

faqs.q: Does a Board of Review appeal pause a Grand Rapids bill?
faqs.a: No. The original bill stays due. If the board changes the value, the treasurer revises the bill within about 30 days of the final report, and refunds go to whoever paid.
